sections.h2: Who bills and values property in Hancock County
sections.html:
Two Sparta offices share the work. One sets what each parcel is worth and approves exemptions. The other prints the bills and banks the payments for the county government and the Hancock schools. Rates come from elsewhere: the county commissioners and the school board settle the mill levy every year.

Sparta is the one incorporated city. Hancock is rural, so most listings are acreage, farmhouses and inherited family places, where the legal description of the land counts as much as the building. Population is 8,682 by the latest estimate, down from 8,735 in 2020.

  • Tax Commissioner: 9031 E. Broad Street, Sparta, phone 706-444-5148. The public counter shuts a quarter hour before five.
  • Tax Assessor: the same street address, phone 706-444-5721.
  • Copies of recorded deeds: the courthouse deed room.

sections.h2: Due dates and what happens if you pay late
sections.html:
Houses, land and business equipment fall due November 15. Manufactured homes fall due April 1. Treat the date printed on your own bill as final, and call 706-444-5148 if anything looks off.

Late real estate bills pick up 1% interest every month. Once three months pass with the balance open, a flat ten percent penalty lands on top. Roughly a month after the deadline, the office can record a tax lien, called a FiFa, in the superior court clerk's docket. These liens are public and credit bureaus can pull them, and the office has no hand in how they are reported. Seizure of the property is the final step, and the office describes it as a last resort.

Hancock County due dates and late costs
Property typeDue dateLate cost
House, land, business equipmentNovember 151% interest monthly, 10% penalty after three months
Manufactured homeApril 110% filing penalty and 1% monthly interest

A mobile or modular unit counts as personal property. It needs a return and a location permit, and the permit is withheld until that year's tax is settled. Past April 1 the county adds a ten percent filing penalty and a monthly one percent interest charge. A unit that stays unpaid can go to auction.

If you plan to sell a manufactured home, get the payoff in writing first, because a buyer cannot get a location permit while the year's tax is open.

You get forty-five days, and the clock starts on the date shown on the notice of assessment, so mail the appeal to the assessors early. When they stand by their number, the case moves to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, then onward to superior court.

The assessors first look at their own figure again and tell you what they decided. If you are still unhappy, a hearing follows before the Board of Equalization, whose members the Grand Jury appoints. Arbitration can replace that hearing. After either result, a written notice to the assessors keeps your case alive for superior court.

Hancock taxes forty percent of a parcel's January market value. Exemptions are subtracted from that slice and the mill rate is applied to the remainder. Ask the assessor's staff to show the math on your own parcel.

Most homeowners begin with homestead. Take the form to the assessor's office. Two conditions apply: you lived in and owned the house when the year began, and the form must be in hand before April. A filing after that point earns nothing until the following year.

  • A granted homestead exemption renews itself as long as you stay put. A move requires a new application for the new address.
  • Owners who reach 62 may apply for an extra exemption. The assessor can say which forms are current.
  • Business owners can ask about freeport relief on inventory, and farm and forest owners can ask about the ten-year conservation use and preferential farm programs.

Returns have a spring window that closes April 1. The first real estate return carries forward at last year's value, so you refile only after building or buying more land. A new return with a lower figure is also how a dispute over the current value begins.

sections.h2: What a typical Hancock County house is worth
sections.html:
Home prices here are among the lowest in Georgia. For 2020 through 2024 the middle owned house is valued at $88,600 and the middle monthly rent is $938. Middle household income is $40,082, and about 79% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.

There were 5,088 homes counted in mid-2025 against 2,922 occupied households, and only 24 building permits were issued in 2025. That gap matters because a vacant or inherited house still produces a tax bill every year. Vacant housing was 32.6% in the 2020 count. If you hold a house like that, call the commissioner before listing to learn what the parcel owes.

sections.h2: Selling with an unpaid tax bill
sections.html:
The bill for a given year lands on the person who owned the parcel when that year opened, which in a sale is normally the seller. The purchase contract and the closing attorney decide how to divide it. Before closing day, request a written payoff from the Sparta commissioner's office.

A buyer's title search will turn up back taxes, and any recorded FiFa must be satisfied at the closing table. With a lien or an unpaid mobile home tax already on file, phone 706-444-5148 early, since the office may levy on property that stays unpaid.

Heirs should also check whose name is on the deed. A warranty deed copy comes from the courthouse deed room, and new homeowners should carry one to the assessor when filing for homestead. Both tax offices share the East Broad Street address in Sparta, and the courthouse is in town as well, so one trip can settle the payoff figure, the exemption status and the deed copy.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal, so a house with old liens or unclear heirs can still close if the title work is clean and the taxes are paid at the table.

  1. Call the commissioner at 706-444-5148 and ask for the balance on the parcel, including any FiFa and any manufactured home tax.
  2. Pull a copy of your deed from the courthouse deed room if heirs or a prior owner are involved.
  3. Stop at the assessor's office to confirm your homestead filing and what the buyer must file.
  4. Give the written payoff to the closing attorney so the taxes come out of the proceeds at the table.

Doing these four things before a buyer is under contract keeps the title search from turning up surprises that could delay the closing.

faqs.q: When do Hancock County property tax bills come due?
faqs.a: November 15 for houses and land, April 1 for mobile homes. Follow the date on your own bill, and call 706-444-5148 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: What does it cost to pay Hancock County property tax late?
faqs.a: Interest of 1% accrues every month on real estate, and a 10% penalty is added when 90 days go by. A FiFa lien becomes possible after a month.

faqs.q: What is the window to dispute a Hancock County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, starting at the notice date. The written appeal goes to the assessors first.

faqs.q: What is the last day to file for homestead in Hancock County?
faqs.a: Get the form to the assessor's office before April arrives. The home must also have been yours, and lived in by you, on New Year's Day. A late form counts toward the next year.

faqs.q: Are mobile homes taxed differently in Hancock County?
faqs.a: Yes. They count as personal property with an April 1 deadline, and no location permit is issued until the year's tax has been paid.
